trackandtracesystem: What is a track and trace system?

It lets you see where every product, asset or shipment is and what has happened to it – from raw material through production, quality checks and dispatch – using QR, barcode, RFID, GPS and IoT scanning at each step.
Which technologies do you use for tracking?
Barcode and RFID scanning, QR codes, live GPS tracking for vehicles and goods, and IoT sensors that monitor temperature, humidity and handling conditions.
Can it work with our existing ERP or warehouse software?
Yes. Our track and trace solutions integrate seamlessly with existing systems, so production and shipment data flows into your ERP without re-typing.
Can our customers see shipment status?
Yes. Automated SMS, email or app notifications share shipment status, delivery confirmations and alerts for delays or route changes.
Does it help with quality and compliance?
Every checkpoint is recorded with digital signatures and audit trails, giving you end-to-end traceability and the reports you need for compliance.
Which industries use your track and trace software?
Manufacturing, logistics and supply chain, warehousing, fertilizer and agrochemical companies, pharmaceuticals, and retail and e-commerce.

qrcodesolution: What is the difference between static and dynamic QR codes?
A static code always holds the same information. A dynamic code can be redirected and tracked after printing, with user analytics and expiry dates. We generate both.
Can you create QR codes in bulk from Excel?
Yes. Our Excel-to-QR service converts product inventories, employee IDs, coupons, tickets and invoices into thousands of unique codes in a few clicks.
Can the QR codes carry our logo and colours?
Yes. Custom QR codes can include your logo, brand colours and unique designs, and they stay high quality and scannable.
Can QR codes help us track products and stop counterfeits?
Yes. Trace-and-track QR codes record product movement across locations, and authentication and encryption help verify genuine products.
What can a QR code link to?
Website URLs, contact details (vCards), Wi-Fi access, product details and pricing, event registrations and more.
